Preface This is the third edition in the National Laboratory of the Rockies’ (NLR’s) Automated Mobility District Implementation Research report series. This overview of NLR’s Phase III research places its focus on system-level elements of an automated mobility district (AMD) beyond the automated driving system (ADS) in each automated/autonomous vehicle (AV). As broad implementation of fully automated mobility systems operating on public roadways edges nearer, with some commercial systems already running or in final startup testing in dozens of major U.S. cities at the time of this report’s publishing, the system-level aspects beyond the maturation of automated driving systems are becoming increasingly critical. The first edition of this effort was published in 2020 and documented insights gained from monitoring 10 early deployment sites of AV technology. The second edition of the catalog was published in 2022, during the COVID-19 pandemic. The second edition updated the progress of the demonstration pilot projects beyond the initial deployment phase and assessed common trends of technology development and deployment. This third edition in the research report series, as in the first two editions, continues to track the 10 early deployment sites, only a few of which are still active. However, the research findings in this overview report also address Phase III research which begins to draw significantly from parallel fields for system-level insights into the future of AV fleets providing public mobility within AMDs, and the associated processes that are critical beyond performance of the ADS. These parallel fields include vehicle electrification, proliferation of on-demand transit, and simulation studies of automated transit networks. The five primary research themes within this third edition are: • Impact and implication of the rise of on-demand transit on AMDs • Challenge of operating multiple AV fleets in an integrated and coordinated fashion • Battery electric vehicle fleet charging strategy and infrastructure • Station/curbfront configurations and operations • Systems engineering methodology for analysis and assessment.
